explanation: new allocates the object on the heap and runs the constructor whose parameters match, leaving the object in a valid starting state.

stem: What is a constructor's one job?
options: To leave the new object in a VALID state
explanation: A constructor has the class's name, no return type, and must establish everything a valid object needs - so no half-built objects exist.

stem: What does 'public string Title { get; }' mean?
options: Title is readable everywhere but settable only in the constructor
explanation: A get-only auto-property can be assigned in the constructor and never after - immutable from then on.

stem: What does ': this(title, "Unknown", 0)' after a constructor signature do?
options: Calls another constructor of the SAME class first
explanation: Constructor chaining: the short constructor forwards to the full one so the real initialisation logic lives in exactly one place.

stem: Book? b = null; What happens on b.Title?
explanation: A null reference points at no object, so using a member throws. b?.Title gives null instead of crashing; the ? annotation makes the compiler warn you first.

stem: Book.Count tracks how many books were created. Why is it static?
options: It belongs to the CLASS - one counter shared by all objects
explanation: Each object could not count its siblings. A static member has one value per class, reached as Book.Count, not myBook.Count.

stem: Inside a method, what does 'this' refer to?
options: The object the method was called on
explanation: this is the current instance - needed mainly when a parameter name shadows a field: this.title = title.

stem: You add a constructor taking two parameters. What happens to the free parameterless one?
options: It disappears - write it yourself if you still want it
explanation: C# supplies a parameterless constructor only when you define NO constructors. Define any, and the freebie is gone.

stem: What is 'new Book("X") { Author = "Me", Pages = 100 }' doing?
options: Running the constructor, then setting public properties
explanation: Object initialiser syntax: constructor first, then the listed property assignments - handy when most values are optional.
